nicholas-nick-schultz.text: Campaign site: "Fighting to make it easier to build needed housing and expand programs to help renters and first-time homebuyers."

Authored AB 1050 to remove restrictive covenants that limit land use on underutilized commercial parcels, to unlock housing. Said that what works in denser Valley Village or Studio City differs from what is appropriate in Shadow Hills, a high fire hazard severity zone.

source.title: Freshman Assemblymember Nick Schultz Brings Experience & Fresh Eyes to the State Legislature (The Planning Report)

nicholas-nick-schultz.text: Said housing now being built is "mostly luxury, market-rate development," and co-authors an Affordable Housing Bond that he describes as the missing piece for building genuinely affordable units.

source.title: Freshman Assemblymember Nick Schultz Brings Experience & Fresh Eyes to the State Legislature (The Planning Report)

nicholas-nick-schultz.text: League of Women Voters Vote411 guide: lists housing affordability and renter protections among his top three priorities, and says "I have and will continue to support legislation that reduces the administrative obstacles and costs to housing production."

source.title: Member of the State Assembly, District 44 - VOTE411 Voter Guide

nicholas-nick-schultz.text: Vote411 top priorities: protecting the environment and addressing the climate crisis; housing affordability and renter protections; economic opportunity and raising wages.

source.title: Member of the State Assembly, District 44 - VOTE411 Voter Guide

nicholas-nick-schultz.text: Vote411: school funding should be based on the total number of enrolled students, for financial stability, and he would explore unrestricted funds to schools. Campaign site calls him a champion for fully funding public education.

source.title: Member of the State Assembly, District 44 - VOTE411 Voter Guide

nicholas-nick-schultz.text: On immigrant legal aid and a $25M DOJ legal defense fund: "These funds will offer direct critical assistance to veterans, students, renters, families, victims of domestic violence, and law-abiding immigrants who are being targeted by the Trump Administration."

source.title: Assemblymember Nick Schultz, Assembly Democrats Pass Legal Defense Fund (press release, Feb 3, 2025)

nicholas-nick-schultz.text: Voted AYE on SB 98 (schools: immigration enforcement notification, urgency) on the Assembly floor, Sept 2, 2025.
Voted AYE on SB 627 (law enforcement: masks) on the Assembly floor, Sept 9, 2025.
Voted AYE on AB 1127 (firearms: converter pistols) on the Assembly floor in June and Sept 2025.
Voted AYE on SB 704 (firearms: firearm barrels) on the Assembly floor, Sept 8, 2025.
Voted AYE on AB 288 (employment: labor organization and unfair practices) on the Assembly floor in June and Sept 2025.
Voted AYE on AB 1340 (transportation network company drivers: labor relations), Sept 9, 2025.

Chair of the Assembly Public Safety Committee; campaign site says he is "working to prevent crime and keep communities safe." Authored AB 1905 (juveniles: custodial interrogation), which passed Public Safety Committee.
On his first day in office he introduced a bill, later law, to protect California's rivers and endangered species from the Trump Administration.
Voted AYE on SB 237 (oil spill prevention: gasoline specifications suspension; CEQA exemptions) on the Assembly floor, Sept 13, 2025.
Voted AYE on SB 71 (CEQA exemptions: transit projects), Sept 2025.
Voted AYE on ACA 8 (congressional redistricting) on the Assembly floor, Aug 21, 2025.
Endorsed by SEIU California, Los Angeles County Federation of Labor, California Professional Firefighters, CalFire Local 2881, and California Teachers Association.
Endorsed by Sierra Club California, Planned Parenthood Advocacy Project Los Angeles County, CA YIMBY, and Stonewall Democratic Club.

carolyn-daniels.text: Vote411 housing answer: "Cut red tape and streamline permitting to reduce the time and cost for the building process" and "Protect Prop 13." Top priorities include funding Prop 36 and enforcing existing laws.

source.title: Member of the State Assembly, District 44 - VOTE411 Voter Guide

carolyn-daniels.text: "Suspend the gas tax, cut the car tax, and reduce the income tax. Defend Prop. 13." Also: "Stop spending money we don't have. Block unfair tax hikes and new taxes."
"Eliminate redundant departments and programs. Stop funding low-priority, vanity projects." Also calls to audit local agencies and NGOs and demand stronger transparency in state spending.
"Cut expensive regulations and streamline permitting to increase supply."
"Support Prop. 36 reforms, back police, and put victims first - not criminals."
"End 'housing first.' Prioritize mental treatment and incarcerate drug offenders. Enforce anti-camping laws."

"California has plenty of natural resources. Sacramento is blocking them. Dump foolish climate policies and make energy abundant again." Also: repeal Prop. 103 and manage forests to prevent wildfires.
"Stop chasing small businesses and the entertainment industry out of state with overbearing permits and red tape."
Vote411 on education: "Families who are involved in their children's education is a proven success," with a focus on accountability, core subjects, and trade classes.

source.title: Member of the State Assembly, District 44 - VOTE411 Voter Guide

carolyn-daniels.text: Vote411 on water: "We don't have a water shortage, We have a storage issue." She would expedite water storage using existing Prop 1 funds rather than seek new taxes.

source.title: Member of the State Assembly, District 44 - VOTE411 Voter Guide

carolyn-daniels.text: Endorsed by the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association PAC (listed for Assembly District 44).

notes: Schultz's positions on health care, abortion (beyond the Planned Parenthood endorsement), and taxes were not found beyond the items listed. Daniels: nothing found on immigration, guns, health care, transportation, or abortion/LGBTQ+.
